criteria.criterion: An `audience` role definition exists in crates/athena-data/src/roles.rs with a goal, a fixed prompt and a cadence. The prompt tells it to read the outcome as its audience would, give a 1–5 rating, and cite evidence for every finding. It passes RoleDefinition::validate and its path is records/roles/audience-<n>.json.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff: roles.rs adds `audience(at)` with a goal, the fixed `AUDIENCE_PROMPT` const (it reads the page as the named reader would on first meeting it, rates 1 (cannot use it) to 5, and cites evidence for every finding) and `cadence_tasks: 20`. The test `the_audience_is_valid_and_asks_for_a_rating_with_evidence` asserts `validate() == Ok(())` and `path() == records/roles/audience-1.json`.

criteria.criterion: A versioned, schema-tagged audience-rating record type holds the target (explainer page URL), the audience (newcomer), a rating (1–5 only), findings that each cite a source, and the time. Out-of-range ratings and findings without evidence are refused.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff: records.rs adds `AudienceRating` with id, at, target, audience, rating and findings[{text, source}]. It has the `athena.audience-rating/1` envelope tag and deny_unknown_fields. `validate()` refuses a rating outside RATING_RANGE (1..=5) and any finding with an empty text or source, and AnyRecord::parse calls it. The tests cover ratings 0, 6 and 255, a blank source and an empty text.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`. Tests cover the role definition, record validation and round-trip, and an end-to-end run with the fake agent over a stubbed page, with no network access. It produces a rating record and the steward sees it.
criteria.evidence: I ran all three commands. The unit tests for the role, the record round-trip and validation, the context schema and audience.rs passed. All 7 tests in tests/audience.rs passed. Among them, `a_run_over_a_stubbed_page_records_a_rating_and_the_steward_sees_it` uses a stub `Page` (no network) and the fake agent. It asserts that the rating record is committed and that the steward run's user prompt contains '## Audience rating', '4/5 from a newcomer', the finding and its evidence. The full `cargo test` run finished without error. Its 54 KB output was saved to a file outside the working directory, which policy blocked me from reading. Athena's own run reported 629 tests passed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`. A test shows the steward's brief or `athena status` output includes the latest audience rating and findings, and that a rating of 2 or lower yields a steward work item. Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`; both are clean.
criteria.evidence: These tests passed. The end-to-end test checks both the steward's brief and `status().audience` (rating, target and findings with evidence). `a_rating_of_two_or_lower_raises_a_work_item_and_three_does_not` tries ratings 1, 2, 3 and 5. It checks that a proposal work item is created only for 1 and 2, cites the rating's path, and appears in status.work_proposals and in the next actions. `the_latest_rating_is_the_one_shown` passed. Clippy with -D warnings and fmt --check produced no warnings or diffs.

findings.evidence: The diff --stat lists these eight files, and none is on the deliverables list. Each is a small change forced by the design. findings.summary: The explainer URL constant cannot be confirmed from the repository.
findings.evidence: `EXPLAINER_URL = "https://doodla.github.io/athena/"`. No doc or workflow in this snapshot states the deployed Pages URL. requirements-map.md D2-1 says nothing is live until the owner enables Pages. If the URL is wrong, `athena audience` will fail at fetch time. The default lives in one place, so it is easy to fix.

findings.summary: The steward brief says a low rating 'has already raised' a work item without checking that one exists.
findings.evidence: `brief_section` infers the work item from `is_low(r.rating)` and does not look it up in records. This holds for every path in this change, because the item is committed with the rating.

summary: This passes. The change adds the `audience` role in code (roles.rs) and an `athena.audience-rating/1` record type. The record refuses ratings outside 1–5 and findings without a source. A new `athena audience` command fetches the page (a stub in tests), runs the model with read-only tools, and commits the rating, its invocation and the role record. A rating of 2 or lower also commits a work item of kind proposal. The steward's brief and `athena status` show the latest rating and its findings. athena.toml and policy.rs are unchanged, which removes the cause of the earlier admission failure. I ran the 7 audience integration tests and they passed. I also ran the unit tests, clippy with -D warnings and fmt --check, all clean. My full `cargo test` run finished without error, but its output was saved outside the working directory and policy blocked me from reading it. Athena's own run reported 629 passing. The design doc, the CHANGELOG and docs/records.md match the code. Two minor points: eight changed files are off the deliverables list, all small changes the design forces, and the hard-coded explainer URL cannot be confirmed from the repository.
